text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- After Kohl's savings package is rejected by Bundesrat upper house of parliament it must be pushed through by a Chancellor's majority -- an absolute majority of all members of lower house of parliament.
- German-Czech declaration will be ready this year.
- Germany will probably not fulfil the Maastricht criteria to qualify for a single currency. The Bundesbank in latest monthly report urges government to keep to savings plans.
- Palestinian president Yasser Arafat will meet Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel for talks in Bonn.
- Only deregulation will create jobs. The liberal Free Democrats (FDP), Chancellor Helmut Kohl's junior coalition partner, urges more market reform.
- Germany appeals to the European Court of Justice against the decision of the European Commission that the regional state of Saxony should pay back subsidies paid to Volkswagen .
HANDELSBLATT

- Bundesrat upper house of parliament rejects government's programme for growth and jobs as expected. The savings packet now depends on a Chancellor's majority in the Bundestag lower house of parliament -- an absolute majority of all members of lower house of parliament.

- Bonn to appeal against decision of European Commission banning subsidy from state of Saxony to Volkswagen to the European Court of Justice. The European Commission will also appeal to the court against the payment of the subsidy.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants less tax burden in planned tax law.
Bundesbank says the economy has improved and urges savings measures. Firmes is east Germany badly affected as wave of bankrupcies rolls on.
- Westdeutschen Landesbank expects less profit for the Bundesbank.
- Despite the continual problem in the apprenticeship market the government will not oblige firms to provide places for trainees.
- Further talks are needed with Prague before post-war reconciliation pact is finalised.
- Gesamtmetall considers dropping Christmas and holiday bonuses for its employees.
- Mannesmann pays one billion marks for 49.8 percent stake in Deutsche Bahn's subsidiary DBKom.
- A new world market leaders in big diesel engines. Finanish Metra-Konzern secures its market.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- The way to reconciliation with the Czech republic is free. Joint declaration should be signed by the end of the year. Even Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber does not expect it to fail and said that his party the Christian Social Union (CSU) agree with 90 percent of the text.
- British government under pressure because of BSE.
- Bonn pays 312 million marks to save the rain forests.
- Bundesrat upper house of parliament votes against Chancellor Helmut Kohl's savings packet.
- The Benelux states practise "wage-dumping" on their domestic markets, according to the premier of Baden-Wuerttemberg, who said this was ruinous for competition in the European Union.
- Record corporate bankrupcies -- 25 billion marks is lost.
- Bonn wants to appeal against European Commission's decision that regional state of Saxony should pay subsidies back to Volkswagen.
- Bonn coalition wants to avoid trade war with the United States.
DIE WELT
- Bundesrat upper house of parliment makes the government savings packet fail again.

- September report of the Bundesbank says that with Germany's public debt it will not fulfil the criteria for a single European currency. It said German public debt would go over the 60 percent mark of gross domestic product (GDP)
- Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber is confident that Germany will reach accord with the Czech republic.
- Record number of bankrupcies in Germany.
